title: Chipped Border Garnet
summary: Tier-1 socketable gem from Act I nodes and chests, adding physical damage in weapons or extra maximum health in armor.
infobox: Act I Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Adds raw physical bite to blades or thickens vitality in plate.
Dug from gravel bars along the Redwater ford.

Pried out of wet river gravel along the Alder Fords by soldiers looking to pad their meager pay. Flawed and dull as dried blood, a chipped garnet still gives a levy blade a little extra bite when hammered into the pommel.

title: Cloudy Fen Beryl
summary: Tier-1 socketable gem from Act I nodes and chests, improving weapon accuracy or expanding maximum mana when set in armor.
infobox: Act I Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Sharpens aim on weapons or expands mana reserves in robes.
Polished by Lantern Passage scribes to read damp ink.

Cloudy green pebbles dredged from Fenwick ditches and sold by hedge-scholars for a handful of coppers. They rarely cut cleanly, yet even a milky beryl steadies a tired archer's aim or holds a spare drop of mana.

title: Bog-Dredged Amber
summary: Tier-2 socketable gem from Acts I–II, infusing weapons with lingering poison damage or granting armor poison resistance.
infobox: Act I–II Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Coats strikes in venom or wards armor against marsh-rot.
Traps prehistoric gnats inside warm golden resin.

Fossilized pine resin pulled from deep bog-trenches, often trapping tiny marsh midges inside its yellow glow. Apothecary apprentices grind the scraps into poultices, while mercenaries socket the whole lumps to weather fen-venom.

title: Alder River Jade
summary: Tier-2 socketable gem from Acts I–II, boosting attack speed in weapons or increasing movement speed when socketed in armor.
infobox: Act I–II Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Quickens weapon swings or lightens boots on muddy roads.
Carved by Thornwick river-pilots as a charm against drowning.

Smooth, cold stones tumbled for centuries along the rocky bed of the Alder River. Ferrymen keep one in their pockets for nimble footing on wet planks, and duelists pay well to have them set into sword hilts.

title: Wardstone Quartz
summary: Tier-3 socketable gem from Acts II–III, adding lightning damage to weapons or granting lightning resistance inside armor.
infobox: Act II–III Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Charges strikes with static or grounds armor against arcs.
Splintered from a ruptured Redmarsh climate monolith.

Chipped from the humming obelisks of the Quartz Plateau after the great storm-rupture. Even a finger-sized prism tingles against bare skin, bleeding off stray static or snapping a bright arc down a spear shaft.

title: Quarry Bloodstone
summary: Tier-3 socketable gem from Acts II–III, providing lifesteal in weapons or a solid boost to maximum health in armor.
infobox: Act II–III Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Siphons vigor on hit or knits torn sinew in armor.
Flecked with crimson iron-oxide from the Deep Quarry.

Dark green jasper flecked with iron-red veins, smuggled out of the Deep Quarry in miners' lunch tins. Pit-fighters prize it above silver because a blade set with bloodstone seems to keep its wielder upright long after he should drop.

title: Glacier-Core Sapphire
summary: Tier-3 socketable gem from Acts II–III, adding cold damage and chill to weapons or cold resistance when fitted into armor.
infobox: Act II–III Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Chills foes on strike or insulates mail against sea-frost.
Brought south by whalers wrecked on the Iron Coast.

Cold as a winter well-bucket, these deep blue stones were traded down from the northern peaks before the passes closed. Set into a breastplate, a single sapphire makes the blistering heat of Redmarsh almost bearable.

title: Caldera Cinder-Ruby
summary: Tier-4 socketable gem from Acts III–IV, packing heavy fire damage into weapons or strong fire resistance into armor.
infobox: Act III–IV Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Ignites weapon blows or turns aside volcanic heat.
Pulled from cooling magma vents below Greystone Bastion.

Formed in the slag-cracks of the Obsidian Caldera where volcanic heat cooks ordinary corundum into glowing crimson. Smiths handle them with iron tongs, as a freshly cut cinder-ruby can scorch a dry leather glove.

title: Tide-Mirror Opal
summary: Tier-4 socketable gem from Acts III–IV, adding astral damage to weapons or mind resistance when set into armor.
infobox: Act III–IV Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Adds armor-ignoring astral force or steadies focus.
Shifts color like deep harbor water before a squall.

Milky coastal stones that flash violet whenever the tide turns or a ward-circle hums nearby. Coastal abbeys set them into iron mirrors to steady the nerves of novices keeping watch over restless crypts.

title: Magnetic Lodestone
summary: Tier-4 socketable gem from Acts III–IV, granting armor penetration in weapons or substantial extra armor when socketed in gear.
infobox: Act III–IV Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Punches through plate seams or reinforces shield rims.
Quarried from the iron-veined cliffs of the Gauntlet.

Dense black iron-ore pulled from the Magnetic Narrows, strong enough to tug nails straight out of a boot heel. Weaponsmiths wedge slivers of lodestone behind blade edges so strikes bite cleanly through riveted plate.

title: Pre-Schism Diamond
summary: Tier-5 endgame gem from Act IV and Hard+, boosting critical strike chance in weapons or granting all resistances in armor.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Finds fatal gaps in armor or wards against every element.
Cut before the First Cataclysm by blind Oakhaven jewelers.

Harder than anything forged since the First Dynasty, these clear stones were pried from pre-schism foundation markers. A jeweler can ruin three iron files trying to facet one, yet veterans kill for a single mounted stone.

title: Heart of the Anchor
summary: Tier-5 endgame gem from Act IV and Hard+, adding heavy fire and astral damage in weapons or large health and mana in armor.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Channels primordial ember into steel or sovereign plate.
Pulsing volcanic glass salvaged from the Obsidian Dais.

Black volcanic glass shot through with a trapped thread of golden ley-light from the Threshold anchors. Quartermasters lock them in lead boxes, claiming they make nearby compasses spin and old wounds ache.

title: Rune of Tally (Tal)
summary: Tier-1 Act I rune that increases gold dropped from kills in weapons or reduces fatigue when socketed into armor.
infobox: Act I Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Marks every fallen foe on the ledger or eases long marches.
First glyph taught to Thornwick toll-clerks.

Scratched onto copper slugs by Thornwick tax-clerks who believed a tidy ledger brought good fortune. Mercenaries hammer the Tally mark into their hilts, joking that if they have to bleed in the mud, the coin better add up.

title: Rune of Iron (Kor)
summary: Tier-1 Act I rune granting armor penetration in weapons or extra physical armor when fitted into defensive gear.
infobox: Act I Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Hardens weapon edges or reinforces riveted mail.
Stamped onto bridge-guard pikes by Master Hobb.

The simplest smithy stamp on the border, denoting pig-iron that passed a cold hammer test without cracking. Levy soldiers press Kor-marked studs into their shields and axe-heads before marching out to the fords.

title: Rune of Draught (Ven)
summary: Tier-2 rune from Acts I–II, boosting mana regeneration in weapons or increasing healing received when set in armor.
infobox: Act I–II Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Draws ambient aether or amplifies apothecary salves.
Inscribed on Widow Marta's copper distillation stills.

Carved on clay cistern-markers to bless dry wells with steady seepage. Field healers and arcanists alike trade silver for Ven stones, appreciating anything that keeps a draught flowing when supplies run thin.

title: Rune of Silt (Silt)
summary: Tier-2 rune from Acts I–II, extending slow duration in weapons or boosting evasion when socketed into armor.
infobox: Act I–II Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Bogs down struck targets or helps scouts slip past blows.
Copied from sunken boundary steles in Redmarsh.

Born among the Redmarsh surveyors who learned how easily wet alkali swallows a careless boot. Bound into gear, the Silt glyph makes an enemy's stride drag like mud while helping its wearer slip clear of heavy swings.

title: Rune of Gale (Gale)
summary: Tier-3 rune from Acts II–III, accelerating cast and attack speed in weapons or improving missile block in armor.
infobox: Act II–III Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Accelerates strikes or deflects incoming arrows.
Chiseled into Oakhaven lighthouse stones.

Etched onto bronze weathervanes along the Oakhaven cliffs to measure sea-squalls. Boarding marines love the Gale mark for turning away arbalest bolts on exposed decks, while casters prize its brisk rhythm.

title: Rune of Lien (Lien)
summary: Tier-3 rune from Acts II–III, amplifying damage-over-time and curses in weapons or extending curse duration in armor.
infobox: Act II–III Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Compounds lingering debts or extends hex bindings.
Used by coastal abbey arbiters to seal deathbed wills.
The jagged notary sign of the Third Dynasty, stamped onto unpaid debt-rolls to bind a debtor's estate past the grave. Necromancers etch it onto wands so their hexes cling like compound interest.

title: Rune of Ward (Ward)
summary: Tier-3 rune from Acts II–III, increasing damage against summons in weapons or granting shadow and astral resistance in armor.
infobox: Act II–III Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Banishes bound horrors or shields against dark rituals.
Carved above the doors of the Sunken Sanctum.

Chiseled into abbey lintels and lighthouse doors to keep restless spirits from crossing the threshold. Veterans marching toward the sunken crypts stitch Ward-stamped discs straight into their gambesons.

title: Rune of Slag (Slag)
summary: Tier-4 rune from Acts III–IV, boosting critical damage in weapons or adding heavy physical armor when set in defensive gear.
infobox: Act III–IV Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Shatters fractured armor or thickens bastion plate.
Quenched in meteor-slag at Forgemaster Vok's hearth.
Cast from cooled furnace dross in Ironcamp's smoky yards, rough-edged and ugly as a broken tooth. Sappers swear a Slag rune hits harder than polished steel simply because it refuses to glance off.

title: Rune of Oath (Oath)
summary: Tier-4 rune from Acts III–IV, strengthening raised servants in weapons or boosting aura effectiveness when set in armor.
infobox: Act III–IV Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Empowers bound watchmen or strengthens squad banners.
Etched onto the brass name-plates of the First Watch.

A double-knotted sigil once sworn over crossed halberds by the Vanguard Company's founders. Whether commanding living levies or bound skeletons, officers socket Oath stones to keep their ranks steady under fire.

title: Rune of Flux (Flux)
summary: Tier-4 rune from Acts III–IV, reducing skill cooldowns in weapons or lowering spell mana costs when fitted into armor.
infobox: Act III–IV Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Cycles invocations faster or conserves arcane reserves.
Decoded from Arch-Mage Malrik's forbidden ley-notes.

Collegium thermodynamicists developed the Flux mark to vent excess pressure from overheated ward-rings. In the field, it lets exhausted casters cycle spells without burning through their last blue draught.

title: Rune of Order (Crown)
summary: Tier-5 endgame rune from Act IV and Hard+, boosting boss damage in weapons or granting high all-resistances in armor.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Purges corruption with star-iron or fortifies against lords.
Struck from the celestial alloy of the Crown of Order.

Modeled after the old First-Dynasty seal of immutable law, struck in cold pale metal that never tarnishes. Only elite vanguard commanders and threshold archivists ever see a genuine Order rune outside a vault.

title: Rune of Ember (Ash)
summary: Tier-5 endgame rune from Act IV and Hard+, granting lifesteal and weapon damage or massive health and armor in defensive gear.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Mineral Nodes, Treasure Chests, Tavern Bounties & Cube Upgrades

p: Feeds on the fallen or turns armor into a living furnace.
Brand of the Obsidian Throne that answers only to will.

Drawn in glowing soot inside the caldera's inner redoubts, humming with the stubborn heat of a banked forge. Those who socket the Ember rune fight like they have nothing left to lose and everything to burn.

title: Chipped Diamond
summary: Tier-1 chipped diamond from Act I shrines and elites; adds undead damage in weapons, an attribute in armor, or all resistances in shields.
infobox: Act I Gem Shrines, Elite Drops & 3-for-1 Transmutation Cube Upgrades

p: Socketable chipped diamond gem.

Tiny, sharp splinters knocked loose from old shrine-markers and swept up by parish sextons. Even a speck of clear diamond makes an undead horror recoil when pressed into a sword fuller or shield boss.

title: Flawed Diamond
summary: Tier-2 flawed diamond from Acts I–II shrines and cube upgrades; boosts undead damage, armor attributes, or shield resistances.
infobox: Act I–II Gem Shrines, Elite Drops & 3-for-1 Transmutation Cube Upgrades

p: Socketable flawed diamond gem.

Clouded by hairline fractures yet hard enough to scratch glass, these stones circulate through border pawnshops after every graveyard skirmish. Shield-bearers prize them as cheap insurance against elemental hexes.

title: Diamond
summary: Tier-3 regular diamond from Acts II–III shrines and cube upgrades; strong undead damage in weapons and balanced resistances in shields.
infobox: Act II–III Gem Shrines, Elite Drops & 3-for-1 Transmutation Cube Upgrades

p: Socketable regular diamond gem.

Cleanly faceted by guild lapidaries in Oakhaven before the evacuation stripped the workshops bare. Set into a kite shield, a regular diamond turns aside fire, frost, and lightning with quiet reliability.

title: Flawless Diamond
summary: Tier-4 flawless diamond from Acts III–IV shrines and cube upgrades; high undead damage, armor stats, or shield all-resistances.
infobox: Act III–IV Gem Shrines, Elite Drops & 3-for-1 Transmutation Cube Upgrades

p: Socketable flawless diamond gem.

Clear as winter ice and worth a small ship's cargo in peacetime. Harborwatch officers traded entire chests of silver for flawless diamonds to fortify their shields against the caldera's elemental storms.

title: Perfect Diamond
summary: Tier-5 endgame perfect diamond from Act IV and Hard+; massive undead damage in weapons, strong armor stats, and top shield resistances.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Gem Shrines, Elite Drops & 3-for-1 Transmutation Cube Upgrades

p: Socketable perfect diamond gem.

Cut with mathematical precision that only First-Dynasty masters or a transmutation cube can achieve. Light passes through it without a single flaw, burning away grave-rot and grounding the fiercest elemental blasts.

title: Chipped Amethyst
summary: Tier-1 chipped amethyst from Act I shrines and elites; improves weapon accuracy, armor strength, or shield defense.
infobox: Act I Gem Shrines, Elite Drops & 3-for-1 Transmutation Cube Upgrades

p: Socketable chipped amethyst gem.

Pale purple shards found in rocky creek beds north of Thornwick. Recruits glue them into buckler rims or bow grips, swearing the dull violet gleam keeps their hands steady when gnolls howl in the fog.

title: Flawed Amethyst
summary: Tier-2 flawed amethyst from Acts I–II shrines and cube upgrades; grants accuracy in weapons, body stats in armor, or shield defense.
infobox: Act I–II Gem Shrines, Elite Drops & 3-for-1 Transmutation Cube Upgrades

p: Socketable flawed amethyst gem.

Slightly deeper in hue than creek-bed chips, these stones turn up in quarry tailings and smugglers' pouches. Mercenaries use them to add a little extra heft to their plate without adding weight to their packs.

title: Amethyst
summary: Tier-3 regular amethyst from Acts II–III shrines and cube upgrades; solid weapon accuracy, armor body bonus, and shield defense.
infobox: Act II–III Gem Shrines, Elite Drops & 3-for-1 Transmutation Cube Upgrades

p: Socketable regular amethyst gem.
Cut into neat six-sided prisms by Redmarsh lapidaries who learned to polish quartz in alkali grit. A regular amethyst sits comfortably in a heavy helm or warhammer, steadying both blow and stance.

title: Flawless Amethyst
summary: Tier-4 flawless amethyst from Acts III–IV shrines and cube upgrades; high weapon accuracy, strong armor stats, and shield defense.
infobox: Act III–IV Gem Shrines, Elite Drops & 3-for-1 Transmutation Cube Upgrades

p: Socketable flawless amethyst gem.

Deep violet stones once reserved for Synod signet rings before the border wars emptied the treasuries. Frontline captains socket them into steel gauntlets and tower shields to hold breaches without flinching.

title: Perfect Amethyst
summary: Tier-5 endgame perfect amethyst from Act IV and Hard+; top weapon accuracy, heavy armor strength, and high shield defense.
infobox: Act IV & Hard+ Endgame Gem Shrines, Elite Drops & 3-for-1 Transmutation Cube Upgrades

p: Socketable perfect amethyst gem.
Rich as bruised plums and heavy in the palm, a perfect amethyst represents weeks of careful transmutation. Veterans who mount one in their gear rarely miss a strike and almost never yield ground.

title: Rune of Eldun
summary: Rank-1 low rune (Req Lv 11) from Acts I–II; adds weapon accuracy or flat defense in armor and shields.
infobox: Act I–II Monsters, Bounty Chests & 3-for-1 Cube Upgrades (Low Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

The first mark taught to apprentice rune-cutters, scratched onto slate tiles until their knuckles ache. Humble as it looks, an Eldun stone steadies a recruit's aim and tightens the rivets on a cheap shield.

title: Rune of Elvar
summary: Rank-2 low rune (Req Lv 11) from Acts I–II; adds weapon damage and accuracy, armor defense, or extra shield block chance.
infobox: Act I–II Monsters, Bounty Chests & 3-for-1 Cube Upgrades (Low Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.
Favored by bridge-guards who spend their shifts catching arrows on tarred wooden shields. Smiths hammer Elvar chips straight into shield bosses to keep the rim from splitting under heavy axes.

title: Rune of Tyra
summary: Rank-3 low rune (Req Lv 13) from Acts I–II; restores mana after every kill whether socketed in a weapon, armor, or shield.
infobox: Act I–II Monsters, Bounty Chests & 3-for-1 Cube Upgrades (Low Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.
Named for a thrifty hedge-mage who hated buying blue draughts from town apothecaries. With a Tyra rune set in his staff, every fallen gnoll paid for the next bolt.

title: Rune of Neph
summary: Rank-4 low rune (Req Lv 13) from Acts I–II; adds knockback to weapons or sturdy flat defense in armor and shields.
infobox: Act I–II Monsters, Bounty Chests & 3-for-1 Cube Upgrades (Low Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.
A blunt, heavy glyph prized by pike-sergeants who want charging boars shoved back into the ditch. Even a light handaxe fitted with Neph hits with the rude jolt of a slammed door.

title: Rune of Aeth
summary: Rank-5 low rune (Req Lv 15) from Acts I–II; improves weapon accuracy or grants steady regeneration in armor and shields.
infobox: Act I–II Monsters, Bounty Chests & 3-for-1 Cube Upgrades (Low Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.
Light and pale as river-chalk, the Aeth mark is stitched into travel cloaks by scouts who cannot afford to stop and bandage every scratch. It keeps the blood moving when the rain turns cold.

title: Rune of Ithos
summary: Rank-6 low rune (Req Lv 15) from Acts I–II; boosts maximum weapon damage or converts incoming damage to mana in armor and shields.
infobox: Act I–II Monsters, Bounty Chests & 3-for-1 Cube Upgrades (Low Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.
Battle-mages swear by Ithos stones during messy ambushes where taking a stray hit is unavoidable. Instead of wasting a bruise, the rune turns a cracked rib into enough mana for a counter-spell.

title: Rune of Talgor
summary: Rank-7 low rune (Req Lv 17) from Acts I–II; adds elemental damage to weapons or high poison resistance in armor and shields.
infobox: Act I–II Monsters, Bounty Chests & 3-for-1 Cube Upgrades (Low Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.
Steeped in bitter fen-herbs before firing, Talgor stones smell faintly of crushed wormwood. Soldiers marching into Redmarsh alkali flats trade good boots just to socket one into their shield.

title: Rune of Ralon
summary: Rank-8 low rune (Req Lv 19) from Acts I–II; infuses weapons with elemental damage or grants strong fire resistance in armor and shields.
infobox: Act I–II Monsters, Bounty Chests & 3-for-1 Cube Upgrades (Low Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.
Quenched in forge-ash until the carved lines glow dull orange in the dark. Ralon runes are standard issue for sappers who expect to walk through burning pitch and cinderling volleys.

title: Rune of Orthan
summary: Rank-9 low rune (Req Lv 21) from Acts I–II; adds elemental damage to weapons or strong lightning resistance in armor and shields.
infobox: Act I–II Monsters, Bounty Chests & 3-for-1 Cube Upgrades (Low Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Wrapped in thin copper wire during the engraving process so the stone drinks stray sparks without cracking. Quarry workers and storm-coast marines keep an Orthan rune handy whenever the sky turns green.

title: Rune of Thulor
summary: Rank-10 low rune requiring level 23 from Acts I–II, adding elemental damage to weapons or high cold resistance in armor and shields.
infobox: Act I–II Monsters, Bounty Chests & 3-for-1 Cube Upgrades (Low Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Chiseled from frost-split slate along the northern river bluffs where winter fog never quite lifts. Scouts socket Thulor into their cloaks before crossing high passes, claiming it keeps rime off their bowstrings and chill out of their knees.

title: Rune of Amnir
summary: Rank-11 low rune (Req Lv 25) from Acts I–II, granting lifesteal in weapons, damage reduction in armor, or thorns damage in shields.
infobox: Act I–II Monsters, Bounty Chests & 3-for-1 Cube Upgrades (Low Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Border veterans prize Amnir above prettier gems because it pays its keep in ugly, drawn-out brawls. Hammered into a sword hilt, it seems to steady a bleeding man's grip; set into a shield, it leaves attackers nursing split knuckles.

title: Rune of Solan
summary: Rank-12 mid rune (Req Lv 27) from Acts II–IV, raising minimum weapon damage or granting flat damage reduction in armor and shields.
infobox: Act II–IV Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Cube Rune Transmutation (Mid Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Struck in heavy brass-toned stone by Redmarsh artificers who hated unpredictable blows. A Solan-socketed blade hits with stubborn consistency, while a breastplate bearing its mark turns aside glancing arrows like a stone wall.

title: Rune of Shaela
summary: Rank-13 mid rune (Req Lv 29) from Acts II–IV, improving weapon accuracy, faster hit recovery in armor, or higher block chance in shields.
infobox: Act II–IV Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Cube Rune Transmutation (Mid Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Light as pumice and slick to the thumb, Shaela stones are traded quietly among duelists and boarding marines. When a heavy club rattles your helm, this little glyph is often the difference between recovering your footing and eating mud.

title: Rune of Dolur
summary: Rank-14 mid rune (Req Lv 31) from Acts II–IV, boosting weapon accuracy or providing steady health regeneration in armor and shields.
infobox: Act II–IV Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Cube Rune Transmutation (Mid Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Field surgeons in Oakhaven used to sew Dolur chips into stretcher-canvas when bandages ran short. It will not reattach a lost finger, but on a three-day march through salt-marsh heat it keeps old cuts from festering.

title: Rune of Helva
summary: Rank-15 mid rune usable from level 1, dropping in Acts II–IV as a prized crafting component for specialized transmutations and runewords.
infobox: Act II–IV Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Cube Rune Transmutation (Mid Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Oddly blank to the naked eye, Helva stones carry no immediate blessing when hammered into plain iron. Quartermasters still lock them in the strongbox, knowing seasoned rune-smiths pay silver to use them as binders in heavier work.

title: Rune of Ioran
summary: Rank-16 mid rune (Req Lv 35) from Acts II–IV, adding weapon damage or boosting strength and maximum health in armor and shields.
infobox: Act II–IV Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Cube Rune Transmutation (Mid Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Quarried from deep ironstone seams where miners work by tallow light until their shoulders knot like oak. Wearing Ioran in your harness lends the stubborn heft of a draft ox, letting tired men hold heavy pavises through long sieges.

title: Rune of Lumix
summary: Rank-17 mid rune (Req Lv 37) from Acts II–IV, increasing weapon damage or granting intellect and maximum mana in armor and shields.
infobox: Act II–IV Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Cube Rune Transmutation (Mid Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Pale as chalked vellum, Lumix stones hum softly whenever a spellbook is opened nearby. Collegium clerks keep them tucked inside ink-stained cuffs to stay sharp through midnight audits and long ward-calibrations.

title: Rune of Kord
summary: Rank-18 mid rune (Req Lv 39) from Acts II–IV, adding weapon accuracy or boosting agility and flat defense in armor and shields.
infobox: Act II–IV Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Cube Rune Transmutation (Mid Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Named after a cliff-runner who outran three tax-cutters across wet shingle without dropping his pack. Kord runes are favored by archers and light scouts who prefer not to be standing where a basalt club lands.

title: Rune of Falkor
summary: Rank-19 mid rune (Req Lv 41) from Acts II–IV, adding solid weapon damage or boosting strength when socketed into armor and shields.
infobox: Act II–IV Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Cube Rune Transmutation (Mid Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Heavy, dark-veined stones stamped with a blunt hammer-mark by Ironcamp foundrymen. Mercenary captains hand Falkor runes to their best breachers, knowing a little extra shoulder behind a warhammer opens stuck gates faster than any key.

title: Rune of Lemur
summary: Rank-20 mid rune (Req Lv 43) from Acts II–IV, dramatically increasing gold found from enemies in weapons, armor, and shields.
infobox: Act II–IV Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Cube Rune Transmutation (Mid Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Every dishonest quartermaster on the Border dreams of a Lemur stone. Though it offers no help in a swordfight, companies that socket it into their gear always seem to pry twice as many crowns out of every fallen raider's purse.

title: Rune of Pulon
summary: Rank-21 mid rune (Req Lv 45) from Acts II–IV, granting strong weapon damage and accuracy or high flat defense in armor and shields.
infobox: Act II–IV Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Cube Rune Transmutation (Mid Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Cut from dense coastal granite that has weathered a thousand winter gales without pitting. Pulon reinforces cheap plate and sharpens dull steel alike, making it one of the most fought-over prizes in any bounty chest.

title: Rune of Umbra
summary: Rank-22 mid rune (Req Lv 47) from Acts II–IV, inflicting open wounds in weapons or granting all-element resistances in armor and shields.
infobox: Act II–IV Super-Uniques, Tavern Bounties & Cube Rune Transmutation (Mid Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Dark as cooled pitch and cold even beside a smelter fire, Umbra stones leave jagged, weeping cuts when mounted in steel. Set into a shield, however, the same grim glyph drinks fire, frost, and lightning without complaint.

title: Rune of Malcor
summary: Rank-23 high rune (Req Lv 49) from Act IV endgame, preventing enemy healing in weapons or reducing magic damage in armor and shields.
infobox: Act IV Obsidian Caldera Bosses, Hard/Nightmare Elites & Pinnacle Vault (High Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Forged in the caldera approaches where shamans and embalmers refuse to let their dead stay down. A single Malcor-marked blade shuts down battlefield mending, turning stubborn cultists into ordinary, manageable corpses.

title: Rune of Istari
summary: Rank-24 high rune (Req Lv 51) from Act IV endgame, boosting magic item find across weapons, armor, and shields.
infobox: Act IV Obsidian Caldera Bosses, Hard/Nightmare Elites & Pinnacle Vault (High Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Talisman-hunters and relic-smugglers trade whole chests of silver for a single Istari chip. It glows faintly near buried vaults and forgotten armories, guiding its bearer toward rare steel that ordinary patrols walk right past.

title: Rune of Guldan
summary: Rank-25 high rune (Req Lv 53) from Act IV endgame, adding high weapon accuracy or raising maximum poison resistance in armor and shields.
infobox: Act IV Obsidian Caldera Bosses, Hard/Nightmare Elites & Pinnacle Vault (High Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Steeped in distilled alkali and sulfur fumes until the stone turns a sickly, indelible green. Veterans marching through spore-choked ruins prize Guldan for hardening their lungs against venoms that drop lesser men in three breaths.

title: Rune of Vexor
summary: Rank-26 high rune (Req Lv 55) from Act IV endgame, granting mana steal in weapons or raising maximum fire resistance in armor and shields.
infobox: Act IV Obsidian Caldera Bosses, Hard/Nightmare Elites & Pinnacle Vault (High Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Warm as a freshly banked coal, Vexor draws stray energy out of every strike to feed hungry casters. Mounted in a shield or cuirass, it lets frontline soldiers wade straight through caldera flames without blistering.

title: Rune of Ohmar
summary: Rank-27 high rune (Req Lv 57) from Act IV endgame, adding heavy weapon damage or raising maximum cold resistance in armor and shields.
infobox: Act IV Obsidian Caldera Bosses, Hard/Nightmare Elites & Pinnacle Vault (High Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Struck from pale alpine quartz that never cracks under a sledgehammer. Weapons fitted with Ohmar cleave through heavy bone and iron alike, while armor bearing its seal shrugs off glacial frost that would snap ordinary steel.

title: Rune of Loral
summary: Rank-28 high rune (Req Lv 59) from Act IV endgame, granting deadly strike in weapons or raising maximum lightning resistance in armor and shields.
infobox: Act IV Obsidian Caldera Bosses, Hard/Nightmare Elites & Pinnacle Vault (High Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Sharp-edged and humming with bottled static, Loral turns clean hits into devastating finishing blows. Storm-coast marines also socket it into their shields so stray lightning arcs ground harmlessly into the flagstones.

title: Rune of Suran
summary: Rank-29 high rune (Req Lv 61) from Act IV endgame, adding solid weapon damage or a large maximum mana pool in armor and shields.
infobox: Act IV Obsidian Caldera Bosses, Hard/Nightmare Elites & Pinnacle Vault (High Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Deep indigo stones recovered from collapsed pre-schism observatories along the eastern ridge. Senior arcanists covet Suran above gold, as a single stone holds enough reserve mana to sustain an entire siege barrage.

title: Rune of Beran
summary: Rank-30 high rune (Req Lv 63) from Act IV endgame, granting crushing blow in weapons or strong damage reduction in armor and shields.
infobox: Act IV Obsidian Caldera Bosses, Hard/Nightmare Elites & Pinnacle Vault (High Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Dense as lead and scarred with ancient siege-marks, Beran is the nightmare of stone golems and armored titans. One lucky swing with a Beran-socketed maul can crack a colossus wide open like a dropped clay jug.

title: Rune of Jahkar
summary: Rank-31 high rune (Req Lv 65) from Act IV endgame, ignoring target defense in weapons or adding high maximum health in armor and shields.
infobox: Act IV Obsidian Caldera Bosses, Hard/Nightmare Elites & Pinnacle Vault (High Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

A ruthless First-Dynasty war-glyph that refuses to acknowledge thick plate or clever parries. Soldiers who socket Jahkar into their armor seem to walk through volleys that should have pinned them to the dirt.

title: Rune of Chamir
summary: Rank-32 high rune (Req Lv 67) from Act IV endgame, freezing foes in weapons or preventing the wearer from being frozen in shields.
infobox: Act IV Obsidian Caldera Bosses, Hard/Nightmare Elites & Pinnacle Vault (High Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

Clear as glacier ice and painfully cold to bare fingers, Chamir locks enemies in brittle rime on contact. Set into a tower shield, it keeps a vanguard captain moving freely even when frost-bells toll overhead.

title: Rune of Zodar
summary: Rank-33 pinnacle high rune (Req Lv 69) from Act IV endgame, granting massive weapon damage or top flat defense in armor and shields.
infobox: Act IV Obsidian Caldera Bosses, Hard/Nightmare Elites & Pinnacle Vault (High Rune)

p: Socketable rune used individually or chained in runeword recipes.

The rarest stone in the Border ledgers, whispered about in taverns by veterans who have never actually seen one. Hammered into steel, Zodar elevates ordinary frontier iron into a weapon worthy of the Threshold itself.
